summary: The Ora 5 is GWM's replacement for the axed Ora hatch: a 4.47m front-drive electric small SUV sold here in two grades, both with the same 150kW motor and 58.3kWh LFP battery. Reviewers agree it is a lot of electric car for the money and unusually quiet at highway speed, and note the rare inclusion of a space-saver spare, but they split sharply on the suspension, which CarExpert calls too firm and Chasing Cars calls floaty yet busy. The consistent criticisms are over-eager driver-monitoring alerts, a touchscreen that swallows the regen and drive-mode controls, and a claimed efficiency figure real-world testing does not reach.
pros: 435km WLTC range from a 58.3kWh usable battery for an under-$35,000 list price, against 345km for the BYD Atto 2 it is aimed at
Seven-year unlimited-kilometre warranty (eight on the battery) with capped-price servicing at $195 a visit, $1,365 across the seven years
Carries a space-saver spare wheel, still uncommon in this class, plus 6kW vehicle-to-load and 120kW DC charging for 10-80% in about 30 minutes
362-litre boot expanding to 1,060 litres with the 60/40 rear seats folded, and a 750kg braked tow rating where the MG 4 manages 500kg and the BYD Dolphin none at all

Both grades ride on the same 18-inch wheels and battery, so the $3,000 step to Ultra buys equipment (panoramic roof, powered tailgate, heated and ventilated seats, dual-zone climate) without costing range
cons: The claimed 15.5kWh/100km is optimistic: CarExpert observed about 18kWh/100km in mixed driving, which cuts real range to roughly 325km
Driver-monitoring and seatbelt warnings misfire repeatedly, and regenerative braking strength is adjustable only through the 14.6-inch touchscreen with almost no physical controls
Ride quality is the main point of reviewer disagreement - firm and bump-sensitive to CarExpert, floaty with mild rear-end instability at speed to Chasing Cars - and neither rates it as settled
Unrated by ANCAP at the time of writing, with testing still under way

GWM publishes no list price at all - only a Victorian drive-away figure ($33,990 Lux, $36,990 Ultra) - so the list prices shown here are backed out of those figures and are estimates, not sourced numbers; the outgoing Ora hatch it replaces was also withdrawn after weak local sales, so expect softer resale than a BYD or MG equivalent
